title: Amoeba Memory Without a Brain
hook: Part one: human memory requires complex neurons, yet a brainless amoeba remembers its meals.
script: Part one: human memory requires complex neurons, yet a brainless amoeba remembers its meals. How can a single cell recall a past food location? Touching food triggers a chemical that permanently widens its microscopic veins. This carves a physical hydraulic highway straight to the nutrition. Its memory is its shape. The altered path persists for up to 72 hours despite constant outside changes. Tear the organism into pieces, and the reconnected fragments still remember where to go. Follow so you do not miss part two.
